# Phantom

> Rust HTTP client with browser connection settings and ordered request headers.
> Package `phantom-http`, library crate `phantom`.

Use documentation for the version being built. Published versions are on
[docs.rs](https://docs.rs/phantom-http/). For Git or path dependencies, read
these files in the matching checkout or run
`cargo doc -p phantom-http --features full --no-deps --open`.

## Start

- [Overview](crates/phantom/src/docs/overview.md): entry point and Cargo features.
- [Getting started](crates/phantom/src/docs/getting-started.md): build and first request.
- [Browser profiles](crates/phantom/src/docs/browser-profiles.md): connection settings and request templates.
- [Requests and responses](crates/phantom/src/docs/requests-and-responses.md): bodies, status codes, and errors.
- [Proxies](crates/phantom/src/docs/proxies.md): routes, proxy credentials, and DNS.
- [Examples](crates/phantom/examples/README.md): programs and run commands.

## When writing code

Check API signatures and feature requirements in this checkout. Start with a
composed browser profile or a short catalog selector such as `chrome-154-windows`.
Attach a default request template for the operation, then reuse the client for
shared pools and session state. Override the template on individual requests
when needed. Preserve header order, select a protocol deliberately, and use
bounded body readers.

For changes to Phantom itself, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Read [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) before upgrading.
